subject: general
question: Which of the following lakes is the largest fresh water lake in north-east India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Loktak Lake**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Loktak Lake** is the largest freshwater lake in northeast India.
 
• It is located in the Indian state of **Manipur**.
 
• The lake is renowned for its **phumdis** (heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil, and organic matter at various stages of decomposition) floating over it.
 
• It serves as a source of water for **hydropower generation, irrigation, and drinking water supply** in the region.
 
• The lake is also home to the **Keibul Lamjao National Park**, the only floating national park in the world, which is the last natural habitat of the endangered **Sangai deer**.
 
• Loktak Lake is an integral part of the culture and economy of Manipur, supporting the livelihoods of a large number of people through fishing and agriculture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kolleru Lake** is one of the largest freshwater lakes in India, located in Andhra Pradesh, but not in northeast India.
 
• **Dal Lake** is a famous lake in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, known for its houseboats and tourism, but it is not in northeast India.
 
• **Pulicat Lake** is the second-largest brackish water lake in India, located on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, and not a freshwater lake in northeast India.
 
• **Northeast India** is a region known for its diverse cultures, languages, and natural landscapes, including several significant water bodies like Loktak Lake.
